name: Hearing the Lord's names, qualities and deeds (śravaṇa)
method_summary: Listening to the names, qualities, deeds and stories of the Lord — from the Bhāgavata and the epics, from devotees and in kathā — with love. First of the Bhāgavata's nine forms (BhP 7.5.23); with singing, a means to devotion even for those living in the world (NBS 37); Garga defines devotion as attachment to hearing his stories (NBS 17); the love of Rāma's stories is the second of the nine in the Rāmāyaṇa tradition.
stage: all; the first of the nine
signs_of_progress: the inauspicious in the heart is shaken off and steady devotion arises (BhP 1.2.16–21)

warnings.text: Stories of lust, wealth, unbelievers and enemies are not to be listened to.

equivalents.note: hearing the Purāṇa recited is the chief form of bhakti-hearing
Vedāntic śravaṇa is study of the Upaniṣads for knowledge of Brahman; bhakti śravaṇa is hearing of the Lord's deeds and names out of love — same word, different object and purpose

notes: One of the Bhāgavata's nine forms of devotion (prc:navadha-bhakti, U07). Exemplar in the tradition's list: Parīkṣit (cpt:nine-exemplars-of-devotion).

name: Singing the Lord's names and praise (kīrtana)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Āḻvārs; Bhakti Sūtras): singing the Lord's names with the mouth while thinking of him with the mind and offering pure flowers (TP 5); the devotees roam the earth singing and dancing (TVM 5.2.1); the name 'Nārāyaṇa' sung as refuge (PTM 1.1); every decad's last verse promises its fruit to those who recite it. The Nārada Sūtra: hearing and singing the Lord's qualities are means even in worldly life (NBS 37); being sung of, he quickly manifests (NBS 80).
signs_of_progress: the Lord manifests and makes the devotee experience him (NBS 80)

name: Remembering the Lord (smaraṇa)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Bhakti Sūtras; Āḻvārs; Gīta Govinda): worshipping the Lord at all times with one's whole being (NBS 79); forgetting him is supreme anguish (NBS 19); remembrance is one of love's eleven forms (NBS 82). Because at death remembrance may fail, the Āḻvārs place the mind at the Lord's feet now and entrust the hour of death to him (Mukundamālā; PAT 4.10.1). The Gīta Govinda is offered to minds that delight in remembering Hari (GG 1.3).

name: Serving the Lord's feet (pāda-sevana)
method_summary: Serving, touching, contemplating and dwelling at the Lord's feet — in the temple image and at his holy places. Fourth of the Bhāgavata's nine forms (BhP 7.5.23). The Āḻvārs make the Lord's feet (tiruvaṭi) their constant refuge: Kulaśekhara asks to lie as a step at the threshold of the sanctum at Tiruvēṅkaṭam; Tiruppāṇ sees the Lord from his feet upward; in Śrīvaiṣṇava temples the Lord's feet (the Śaṭhāri, named after Nammāḻvār) are placed on the worshipper's head.

equivalents.note: receiving the Lord's feet on the head is a ritual form of feet-service
some commentators include visiting the Lord's holy places under feet-service

notes: One of the Bhāgavata's nine forms of devotion (prc:navadha-bhakti, U07). Exemplar: Lakṣmī.

name: Worship of the Lord (arcana, pūjā)
method_summary: Worship of the Lord in his image or symbol with flowers, water, lamps, food and praise, according to rule or with simple love. Fifth of the Bhāgavata's nine forms; Vyāsa's definition of devotion is attachment to worship (NBS 16) and worship is one of love's eleven forms (NBS 82); the Tiruppāvai's girls come pure and strew pure flowers (TP 5).
notes: One of the Bhāgavata's nine forms of devotion (prc:navadha-bhakti, U07). Exemplar: King Pṛthu. Detailed rules of worship belong to the Pāñcarātra and Vaikhānasa entries (U08).

name: Obeisance and adoration (vandana)
method_summary: Bowing, prostrating and adoring the Lord with joined palms. Sixth of the Bhāgavata's nine forms. Tamil toḻutal: 'O my mind, worship his radiant feet and rise' (TVM 1.1.1); the Gītā's 'bow to me' (BhG 9.34).

equivalents.note: Pāśupata prostration as an offering to Rudra

notes: One of the Bhāgavata's nine forms of devotion (prc:navadha-bhakti, U07). Exemplar: Akrūra.

name: Servitude to the Lord (dāsya)
method_summary: Relating to the Lord as his servant and serving him. Seventh of the Bhāgavata's nine forms. For the Āḻvārs servitude (aṭimai) is the soul's nature: 'at all times without break we must do faultless service' (TVM 3.3.1); the drum the girls ask is service for seven times seven births (TP 29); the Āḻvārs ask to serve the Lord's servants. The Nārada Sūtra: love as an eternal servant (NBS 66).

equivalents.note: Śrīvaiṣṇava kaiṅkarya is service as the soul's goal, grounded in the Āḻvārs' aṭimai

notes: One of the Bhāgavata's nine forms of devotion (prc:navadha-bhakti, U07). Exemplar: Hanumān.

name: Friendship with the Lord (sakhya)
method_summary: Relating to the Lord as a trusted friend. Eighth of the Bhāgavata's nine forms; friendship is one of love's eleven forms in the Nārada Sūtra.
notes: One of the Bhāgavata's nine forms of devotion (prc:navadha-bhakti, U07). Exemplar: Arjuna, whom Kṛṣṇa calls 'my devotee and friend' (BhG 4.3). The Gauḍīya sakhya-rasa (trm:sakhya-rasa, U16) systematises it.

name: Offering oneself to the Lord (ātma-nivedana)
method_summary: Handing over oneself and all one has to the Lord. Ninth and last of the Bhāgavata's nine forms. 'Give up everything; give your life to the one who owns release' (TVM 1.2.1); 'I, your servant with no other refuge, have entered beneath your feet' (TVM 6.10.10); having offered self, world and Veda the devotee has no care for worldly loss (NBS 61).

equivalents.note: self-offering and taking refuge coincide in the Āḻvārs' surrender verses
the Śrīvaiṣṇava rite of surrender, grounded in TVM 6.10.10

notes: One of the Bhāgavata's nine forms of devotion (prc:navadha-bhakti, U07). Exemplar: Bali.

name: The Mārkaḻi vow of the Tiruppāvai (pāvai nōṉpu)
method_summary: In the month of Mārkaḻi the girls rise before dawn, wake one another, bathe, and go singing the Lord's names to his house; during the vow they take no ghee or milk, wear no kohl or flowers, do nothing forbidden, speak no evil, and give alms; they worship with pure flowers, singing and meditation. In the tradition the Tiruppāvai's thirty verses are sung daily throughout Mārkaḻi, one for each day, in temples and homes.
duration: the month of Mārkaḻi (mid-December to mid-January)

equivalents.note: the Śaiva Mārkaḻi dawn vow of Māṇikkavācakar's Tiruvempāvai

notes: The dietary abstentions are a vow of restraint, not a prolonged fast.

name: Praying for the Lord's welfare (maṅgaḷāśāsana)
method_summary: Out of overflowing love, the devotee prays for the Lord's own long life and safety — 'many years, many years' (Tiruppallāṇṭu) — rather than for anything for himself, and invites other devotees to join. The Āḻvārs' hymns to each temple are called their maṅgaḷāśāsana of that site; the Tiruppallāṇṭu opens Śrīvaiṣṇava daily worship.
notes: Hagiographic occasion: Periyāḻvār feared the evil eye on the Lord who had appeared on Garuḍa (tea:guruparampara-prabhavam-arayirappati:periyalvar).

name: Awakening the Lord at dawn (tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci)
method_summary: At dawn the Lord in the temple is roused with song — the sun has risen, the gods and sages wait at his door — and the singer asks to be made servant of his servants. Toṇṭaraṭippoṭi's ten verses are sung daily at Śrīraṅgam and other Śrīvaiṣṇava temples.
notes: Cf. the Sanskrit suprabhātam (src:venkatesa-suprabhatam, U14) and the Śaiva Tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci of Māṇikkavācakar (U18).

name: Sung and enacted recitation of the Prabandham (araiyar cēvai)
method_summary: Hereditary temple singers (araiyars) sing the Āḻvārs' verses with gesture and dance before the Lord, above all during the recitation festival; the tradition traces the service to Nāthamuni, who set the hymns to music.
notes: Surviving at Śrīraṅgam, Śrīvilliputtūr and Āḻvār Tirunagari (as recalled; moderate).

name: The annual festival of reciting the Prabandham (adhyayana-utsava)
method_summary: An annual festival of about twenty days in the month of Mārkaḻi, around Vaikuṇṭha Ekādaśī, in which the whole Prabandham is recited before the Lord — the 'ten days' and 'ten nights' (pakal pattu, rā pattu) — ending with the Tiruvāymoḻi and the enactment of Nammāḻvār's liberation. The tradition says Tirumaṅkai began it at Śrīraṅgam and Nāthamuni restored it.
notes: Details (duration, the reenacted liberation of Nammāḻvār on the last day, opening with Tiruneṭuntāṇṭakam) recalled with moderate confidence.

name: Receiving the Lord's feet (caṭāri / śaṭhāri)
method_summary: In Śrīvaiṣṇava temples, the priest places on the worshipper's head a crown-like vessel bearing the Lord's feet, called after Śaṭhakopa (Nammāḻvār), who is held to be the Lord's feet — refuge at the feet received through the Āḻvār.
notes: Exact explanation of the name varies; moderate confidence.

name: Pilgrimage to the divine sites and maṅgaḷāśāsana
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Āḻvārs): the Āḻvārs travelled to the Lord's temples and sang each one — Tirumaṅkai some eighty — longing to be born even as a fish or a step at Tiruvēṅkaṭam, seeing the Lord at Śrīraṅgam from feet to face, calling the reclining Lord at Kuṭantai to rise and speak; the sites they sang became the 108 divya-deśas.

name: Recitation and contemplation of the tirumantra
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Āḻvārs): Tirumaṅkai, given the eight-syllable mantra by the Lord himself (the tradition's account), sang that he had searched and found the name 'Nārāyaṇa', which gives every good (PTM 1.1).

name: Taking refuge in the Lord (śaraṇāgati)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Āḻvārs): the devotee with no other refuge settles beneath the Lord's feet, naming Śrī who never leaves him (TVM 6.10.10); clings to him though he cause grief (PT 5.1); pleads the unbreakable relation (TP 28); entrusts the hour of death to him in advance (PAT 4.10.1).

name: Devotion to the teacher (guru-bhakti)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Āḻvārs; Bhakti Sūtras): Madhurakavi's devotion to Nammāḻvār — his teacher's name sweeter than Kṛṣṇa, 'I know no other god', the teacher as mother and father; the Nārada Sūtra: devotion comes chiefly by the grace of great souls, who are not different from the Lord.

name: Holy company (satsaṅga)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Bhakti Sūtras; Āḻvārs): the company of the great is hard to gain, unfathomable and unfailing, won by the Lord's grace; strive for it alone (NBS 39–42); the Tiruppāvai's girls first wake their companions before going to the Lord (TP 6–15).

name: Shunning bad company (duḥsaṅga-tyāga)
method_summary: Avoiding in every way the company that breeds desire, anger, delusion, loss of memory and of understanding and utter ruin — small ripples that become an ocean through association (NBS 43–45); likewise not listening to talk of lust, wealth, unbelievers and enemies (NBS 63).

name: Offering all conduct to the Lord (tad-arpitākhilācāratā)
method_summary: Dedicating every action to the Lord (Nārada's own definition of devotion, NBS 19); having so offered all conduct, even desire, anger and pride are to be turned toward him alone (NBS 65); until love is attained, action continues with its fruit given up (NBS 62).

equivalents.note: the Gītā's offering of all acts to the Lord (BhG 9.27)

name: Reflecting on the scriptures of devotion
method_summary: The scriptures of devotion are to be reflected upon and the acts that awaken devotion done (NBS 76); no half-moment wasted waiting for a better time (NBS 77); but disputation is avoided (NBS 74–75).

name: The devotee's conduct: non-violence, truth, purity, compassion, faith
method_summary: Carefully keeping non-violence, truthfulness, purity, compassion, faith and the other virtues (NBS 78); giving up pride and hypocrisy (NBS 64), since the Lord dislikes pride and loves humility (NBS 27).

name: Resorting to solitude (vivikta-sthāna-sevana)
method_summary: Among the marks of the one who crosses māyā: resorting to a solitary place, uprooting worldly bonds, giving up acquiring and keeping (NBS 47); with giving up sense-objects and attachment, a means to devotion (NBS 35).

name: Singing the Gīta Govinda (aṣṭapadī)
method_summary: Singing Jayadeva's twenty-four songs in their rāgas and tālas before the Lord and in devotional gatherings: daily in the Jagannātha temple at Purī (the temple singers' service), in Kerala temples as aṣṭapadī (sopāna saṅgītam) and in the Kṛṣṇanāṭṭam built on the Kṛṣṇagīti, in South Indian bhajana, and among the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas; also danced (Odissi and other forms). The poem offers itself to those whose minds delight in remembering Hari.

warnings.text: The love-play of the Lord is not to be imitated, even in mind, by one who is not a lord; one who does so perishes, like one who drinks poison imitating Rudra.

notes: Recorded details of temple use (the Purī order attributed to Gajapati Pratāparudra; Kerala temple practice) recalled with moderate confidence.
